A Chinese Hunter pulled my arms behind my back and handcuffed me. Judging from how they were suddenly doing this, the middle-aged man seemed to be Unawakened.
“I should say that it’s very nice to meet a person from my own country while abroad, but who are you again?”
As I approached the table, the middle-aged man stood up, the corners of his mouth twisting.
“I once had a position in the Hunter Association. Thanks to you-.”
“Ah! I remember! You’re Wanyong-ssi. Surname Lee, right? Wow, I was wondering how the Chinese knew me inside out; I see it’s because you really lived up to your name[1].”

There were many people at the hospital who knew about my Poison Resistance, so that was one thing, but the Sprout skill was top secret. I’d informed only the Association as part of negotiations for the Awakening Center.
At my words, Lee Wanyong scowled darkly and seized me by the collar.
“You bastard, you’re all talk!”
“How could I be as much talk as you are? How much did you boast? Huh? Your face is so bright that you must’ve been treated well.”
“I was the Hunter Association’s human resources department head-!”
“Yes, Wanyong-ssi. I told you I knew you.”
With the way his face was screwed up, I was going to get beaten.

“If you betrayed your country and found yourself a place, then why didn’t you enjoy it quietly instead of meeting me? What all have you sold out? If you were in the HR department, you must’ve given up all the Association Hunters’ abilities. Isn’t it a relief that Chief Song-nim isn’t a part of the Association? There’s no way you could’ve just been kicked out from the Association; they must’ve written a contract to keep your mouth shut, so I guess you got it nullified.”

Just in case, I turned off Curse Resistance for a while. Because if Wanyong-ssi suddenly whirled around and hugged me, the curse would be lifted. At my words, Wanyong-ssi spat insults at me. Had the curse he got for breaking his contract not been lifted? He seemed to be physically unharmed, so what curse was it?
“I worked so hard from the early days of the Association to establish myself!”

“I heard about that. They said that you played a major role in driving out the initial members? Normally, if you drive people out, you’ll also be driven out—what goes around comes around, you see? You reaped what you sowed.”

Had he met with me just to vent his anger? I didn’t think so. I hadn’t thought the assholes ousted from the Association who escaped prison sentences would live quiet lives, but I hadn’t thought they’d sell information this quickly. Although even if I had known, I would have had no real way to stop them.
‘They would’ve written a fairly strong contract.’

But the Association had to pay attention to the matter of human rights as well. They couldn’t use something at the level of blowing your head off if you blabbed. That was why when you registered as a Hunter, even if they noticed you hiding skills or abilities, they’d normally just overlook it.

“Do you have any other friends who came along with you? Or how about the former MKC side? I heard they also joined hands with China. Did you sell a lot of information about the rearing facility? What about Haeyeon?”
When I mentioned Haeyeon, the hand gripping my collar grew tight. Wanyong-ssi tugged, pulling me halfway up onto the table. The sharp corners of the table hurt a little.
“Elder or younger brother, they’re both bastards…….”
The asshole gritted his teeth and muttered. Why was Yoohyun-ie coming up here?
“Why are you finding fault with someone’s little brother?”
“Don’t you know that young fool Han Yoohyun was brought in by the Association when he’d just Awakened? But then, that bastard went and caused chaos.”
…I knew the association temporarily sheltered him, but—chaos? When I unconsciously frowned, that jerk Wanyong started blustering. As I thought, he was twice the talker I was.

“I tried persuading him to join the Association because he was a minor and an S-rank. I told him that if people learned that a child who had nothing was an S-rank Hunter, not even his family would be safe.”

…I recalled how Yoohyun-ie, who’d appeared after going missing for a few days, had coldly turned away from me. Was it the Association bastards who’d been spewing nonsense? Of course, they hadn’t been wrong. If Yoohyun-ie and I had been on good terms, there would’ve definitely been people who would take me hostage to gain leverage over the S-rank Hunter without a single backer.
Still, he threatened a kid like that? Was that something an adult should do?
“Like you said, asshole, he was a child. But you tried to make him bow down to you by bringing up his family? You rotten fucking son of a bitch.”

To think he’d tried to make a child falter by going for his weak point. It was disgusting beyond words. It was disgusting for adults to take another adult’s families hostage, even, but a minor’s? I grew heated. That son of a bitch spoke provokingly.

“Did you know that little idiot wiped out the temporary accommodations for high-rank Awakened people and even knocked out all the Association-affiliated Hunters? We were trying to persuade him as nicely as possible. Fuck, and then that bastard said he was going to make his own guild and threatened to kill us if we got in his way-.”
“He did a good job, then.”

Our Yoohyun-ie was so smart. Before he got Seok Simyeong’s help, I’d worried about how he’d be able to prepare to create a guild on his own, but to think the son of a bitch in front of me had tried pushing him around. I was glad the kid hadn’t had to suffer that.

“You failed to take his family hostage, and in the end he was an S-rank Hunter without any weaknesses, so you must’ve been really freaking out, huh? If things went wrong, you’d all get killed and you wouldn’t even be welcome if you fled abroad, so if you wanted to live, you had to clean up after my little brother. Thank you for that, really.”

A threat like that wouldn’t work once the guild had established itself. Because it could impact the guild badly at any moment. But before that, well, he had nothing to lose, even if they desperately told the whole world. There was a possibility that it’d be caught as a weakness once the guild had been set up, but wouldn’t Seok Simyeong have handled that sort of thing well?

Wanyong kept cursing away. My eyes flicked around, examining our surroundings. Two Hunters were standing guard in front of the door. Beside them, Chu Huayun looked bored. There was also one standing next to the table, but they weren’t right by us. And they didn’t look like a high-rank Hunter, either.
“So, Wanyong-ssi, do you still keep in touch with Korea? The Association’s been cleared out, but we haven’t turned everything over, so I’m worried.”

It was just the critical parts that had been axed. There’d been internal cleanups since then, but it was impossible to wipe out everything. Iron table corners. Would it work? I should’ve worked out more diligently.
“It’s hard for me to escape from here anyway, so please, let’s hear who the spy is. …Ah, this posture’s uncomfortable.”
Grumbling ‘let go of my collar’, I sat down naturally on top of the table.
“You think I’ll tell you that? Still, Director Han, I can at least give you some advice.”
Hm, could this be that sort of thing? The person who changed sides first going ‘hey, if you want this to be easy~’, that sort of thing. I’d seen the friendly act sometimes.
In any case, this fucker would continue to steal information from Korea, and he’d threatened my baby brother.
“Honestly, should a person giving advice be picking a fight? You’re terrible at your job.”
“You picked a fight first, you know! After you stuck by S-ranks like that only to get dragged here in the end, I wanted to see-.”

I threw my upper body backwards. My back touched the table, and the son of a bitch holding my collar staggered. At the same time, I kicked off the table, one leg flying up. My folded knee hit the back of the bitch’s neck, and rolling completely as if in a somersault, my knee—and the fucker’s neck—drove into the corner of the table.
Kwang!
Along with that sound, I heard his neck snap. A Chinese Hunter who dashed forward belatedly grabbed me. Wanyong-ssi’s body slid down the table and crumpled.
“Get a hea—No, he died instantly!”

Even just being hit by a knee kick was dangerous. With the iron table’s help on top, if I got him properly, an Unawakened person was unlikely to survive. Chu Huayun, walking over leisurely, nudged the fallen Wanyong-ssi with his toes. Then he turned his gaze to me. I gave him a smile that asked if he had a problem with this.
“You’re more merciless than you look.”
“Is there any reason to keep a son of a bitch who sells out his country alive? Besides, he even touched my brother.”

If he was left alive, he might even get his hands on the actions being taken in Korea to save me. I should dispose of him while I had the chance. Chu Huayun reached out a hand and snatched me by the nape. As if dealing with a rat, he lifted me with ease and threw me to the ground.
“Ah, shit.”
That hurts, you know. With my wrists bound behind my back, I had no choice but to fall on the floor defenselessly.

“An F-rank Hunter who hasn’t even been Awakened for half a year, who’s been wrapped in the protection of the Haeyeon Guild Leader. A special support type, at that. And yet, you killed someone like it was nothing.”
“It may not have been long since I Awakened, but it isn’t just a few difficulties I’ve faced. I lived a hard life before that, too. Even just in terms of kidnappings, I’m an old hand at this.”
If you added in the times before I regressed, you’d need over ten fingers.
“And even if I tolerated everything else, I can’t tolerate someone laying a hand on my brother—on my kids.”
My eyes met the gaze looking down at me coldly.
“If you touch my kids, then S-rank or not, you die.”
Chu Huayun laughed soundlessly, perhaps thinking it was a bluff. I mean it, though. Then the bastard gently placed a foot on my right leg.
“A man died on my watch, so you should pay the price.”
“Bullshit, it didn’t matter to you whether he died or not.”

We were standing apart and he was looking away, but he had the title of S-rank. If he’d tried to stop me, it wasn’t impossible for him to succeed, but he’d crawled over as sluggishly as a turtle without even lifting an eyebrow—what was he talking about? But Chu Huayun didn’t even pretend to hear me.

His foot applied pressure. In an instant, the bone in my leg snapped. For a moment, my vision went white. I clenched my teeth and managed a sharp exhale when he pressed further down as if to crush the broken bone altogether.
“Augh, urgh! Fuck…….”
My whole body shook from the intense agony. Without me even knowing it, my fingers were scrabbling at the ground. This crazy asshole, nghh…….
The foot bearing down on my leg just barely pulled away, and the bastard took out a potion. When I saw it, a chill went down my spine.
“W─ Wait a second! If you─ use a potion now…….”

If you used a potion lower than high-grade on a bone that wasn’t simply broken but shattered to pieces, the injury wouldn’t heal properly. Because it was recovered while it was a mess, curing it completely would instead become more difficult. …That was a fact I knew from experience.
But the bastard poured the potion on my leg as it was. The pain lessened but didn’t disappear entirely. I tensed my injured leg, trying to move it.
“…Ugh.”
Tingling pain shot through it. Seriously, what a son of a bitch.
“I’ll show you to where you’ll be living from now on. Follow me.”
The asshole walked past me towards the door. Hey, you son of a bitch!
“I can’t even stand, you know?!”
“Then you’ll have to crawl.”
The way he looked down at me felt incredibly awful. Sigma was so nice compared to this bastard. And the food was better than this place’s, too. I really did miss our Moon.
“They say it takes one to know one—do you think I’m a dog because you’re one yourself? Telling me to crawl, what bullshit. Bark bark. I cursed you just now. What did I say?”
Chu Huayun’s eyebrows drew together in a slight frown.
“Did you not understand that? If you’re not a dog bastard, then… meow? Myaow. If not this, then what? Mae-e-e?”
“Get him up.”
A Chinese Hunter helped me up at Chu Huayun’s order. When I put my right foot on the ground, I felt terrible pain. Chu Huayun approached the door. No, how can I wa…….
The Chinese Hunter’s hand pushed against my back, hurrying me on. I reflexively took a step, and then—kudangtang—toppled forward.
“I can’t wa-.”
“Get back up.”

A cold order was given. What… oh, jeez. Even among all the sons of bitches I’d met, this son of a bitch was among the top-ranked. No wonder even Bak Hayool walked on eggshells around him; he was no ordinary crazy asshole. Once again, I picked myself up and took a step with gritted teeth, only to collapse in less than two steps.
“Get up.”
Ah, I want to go home.
“Chao Lake Special District is a place where Awakened people who need dedicated supervision and observation are sent.”

That bastard Chu Huayun showed me around unexpectedly properly. Ignoring how he was forcibly dragging around a person who was struggling to walk, there was the occasional mention of something I should listen carefully to.
“In particular, the Special Awakened People Management Facility 1 on Mushan Island[2] holds Awakened people with rare or important skills.”

What, was he telling me to steal them away? But surveillance was undoubtedly thorough. There were three S-rank Hunters alone currently staying in this place, including Chu Huayun and the one called Guan niangzi. Apparently they were on a rotation, but three or more were always on call. In addition, he said they could request assistance from Shanghai in case of emergency.
‘Shanghai’s a really big city, so they must have three or four S-ranks.’

How close was it to here? For now, I should assume seven or more S-rank Hunters could gather within a few hours. On the other hand, the S-rank Hunters coming here from our side… would be five, at the most? Since a few would have to remain in Korea.
“This is the second restaurant.”
“…I’m not interested.”
Just let me go, you son of a bitch. My back was soaked with cold sweat. Chu Huayun looked over at me and smiled.
“If you can adjust your Poison Resistance, I’ll give you painkillers.”
“I can’t. Besides, why would I trust you and take them? Do you actually think I’m a fucking dog?”

No, even a dog wouldn’t eat them. How could I know if they were real painkillers, or some truth serum-type or other suspicious drug? How could I accept it readily? That asshole Chu Huayun started walking again. As I turned, I fell again. I didn’t know how many times it had been. Wouldn’t my whole body be covered with bruises?
‘He’s trying to discourage me, the damn asshole.’
If I just cried that I’d been wrong, he might let me off at this point. That would be easier, but─ dammit. He could kiss my ass.

I was dragged from inside the building to the outside as well. The sun had gone down at some point and cold wind from the lake swept over my body. Stairs, these goddamn─ stairs. Still, if they thought my head was going to hit an edge on the stairs, they caught me. I went up the stairs, all but falling up them, and stood on the observation deck overlooking the lake. No, I crumpled.
Huddled against the railing, I glared at the crazy son of a bitch.
“You have a talent for torturing people, then?”

He hadn’t simply caused me agony, he’d made me exhausted. Chu Huayun leaned back against the railing and took out something resembling a cigar. Had cigarettes for high-rank Awakened people already come out in China? Or was he just setting the mood? With practiced motions, he cut the end, lit it up, and held it in his mouth.
“We’re going to be seeing each other for a long time, so I want to make sure this will be engraved in your mind.”
“Engraved? You’re making me laugh.”
I snorted. He sure dreamed big.
“When I go back home, I’m going to get completely cured and live well. You can try, but this is nothing. It’s really nothing at all.”

There was only one guy who could break my heart badly enough that I couldn’t heal. Compared to that, this was seriously nothing much. I squinted, staring at the black, rippling water’s surface through the railing. The light from the watchtower shone, stretched out, and moved away.
I wonder what everyone’s doing around now.

[1] Fictional character Lee Wanyong shares his name with Korean politician Lee Wanyong, who (along with four others, collectively known as the Five Eulsa Traitors) signed the Japan-Korea Annexation Treaty along with further treaties that placed Korea under Japanese colonial rule. The name is all but synonymous with “traitor”.

[2] Given here as 노산도 (Nosan-do), Geunseo’s presumably talking about the real-life Mǔshān Island (姥山島／姥山岛, Mǔshān-dǎo), one of two islands located in Cháo Lake (巢湖, Cháo-hú). You can read more about Mǔshān Island on Chinese Wikipedia (no English available, sorry!) and Cháo Lake on English Wikipedia. (The island’s name would more accurately be transcribed in Korean as 모산도 (Mosan-do), since it uses the Mǔ reading of the 姥 character, corresponding to the Korean reading Mo. The No reading Geunseo used comes from 姥’s alternate reading Lǎo, which corresponds to the Korean reading Ro that then turns into No at the start of words.)
